Signs of the World

Hospital

History

In 1864, the US Army began marking its hospitals with a yellow flag bearing a green H. The same year, the first Geneva Convention adopted the red cross to protect medical care on the battlefield. The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends two blue hospital signs. One has a white H and the other shows a bed and a red cross.

Adoption

Medical care is a critical human need around the world. Road signs often mark hospitals with a white cross or H. The American Red Cross has objected to the generic use of a red cross, citing the Geneva Convention and US trademark law. A white cross on green is the ISO 7010 symbol for first aid.
